# First archive

## 1. Log in, once, by hand

```bash
instagram-archiver login
```

A Chromium window opens on the Instagram login page. Log in yourself,
including any two-factor step. **Nothing is typed for you**, and neither your
password nor your session is read by the tool. The browser keeps the session
in a per-user directory and every later run reuses it.

## 2. Try a few posts first

```bash
instagram-archiver profile https://www.instagram.com/someaccount/ --max-posts 3
```

Three posts take about a minute and a half and tell you whether the account is
visible to you at all.

## 3. Archive the profile

```bash
instagram-archiver profile https://www.instagram.com/someaccount/
```

Photographs only, by default. Add `--videos` to save videos too:

```bash
instagram-archiver profile https://www.instagram.com/someaccount/ --videos
```

Progress is printed after every post:

```text
  [######..................]  26.7%  12/45 posts | 148 files | 09:12 elapsed | ~25:18 left
```

Leave it running. Re-running is cheap - everything already in the index is
skipped - and `--resume` skips complete posts without even visiting them.

## 4. See what you got

```text
ig_archiver/
  archive.log
  someaccount/
    2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_01.jpg
    2026-08-17_DcJvpIRjwJa_02.mp4
    metadata/
      index.csv   index.json
      posts.csv   posts.json
```

[The full layout](output.qmd) explains every file.

## Where next

- Only want to know *what* an account posted? [`scan`](commands.qmd#scan) does
  that in a tenth of the time, without downloading anything.
- Reading someone else's public account? Read
  [what is visible, and to whom](visibility.qmd) first - some numbers are a
  lower bound rather than the truth.
